newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steady to lower, demand wanes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steady to lower, demand wanes.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices were unchanged to down slightly Thursday, with fading East Coast utility demand pressuring grades in New York, while prices at the U.S. Gulf held steady, industry sources said.

"Crude is still near $20, we're competitive with gas and there's been decent bunker demand, but this is the slack (spring) period, and we need some demand," said one cash trader, adding resid prices should be near bottom.

In New York Harbor, physical one percent again eased slightly to $14.25 a barrel, with May one percent paper little changed in the $14.20-40 area. Traders said June paper sold at $14.85, also flat from Wednesday despite softer crude.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour held steady at $15.25.
High sulphurs in New York also were little changed, with 2.2 percent still talked around $14, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices again were stable, with one percent still pegged at $14.50 and three percent still straddling $13.25.

New York city gate swing gas prices gained five cents Thursday to the mid-$2.40s/mmBtu, or $15.44 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, firmed a couple of cents to $2.18/mmBtu, or $13.73 a barrel.
